prompt:
You are a careful equity research analyst. Assess the competitive advantages (economic moat) and pricing power of the publicly listed company "Trane Technologies plc" (ticker TT), and list its competitors. Use the most recent information you know. Never invent figures: use null when unsure. Be specific (products, numbers, years).

Reply with ONLY one JSON object, no other text, in exactly this shape:
{
 "name": "official company name", "ticker": "TT", "industry": "industry in a few words",
 "markets": ["the main product markets it competes in"],
 "mission": {"statement": "the company's own official mission statement, word for word as it publishes it; null if you are not sure of the exact wording (never paraphrase here)",
             "source": "where it is published, e.g. company website or 2025 annual report, or null",
             "plain": "what the mission means, in one short simple sentence"},
 "about": {"plain": "3-4 short sentences explaining what the company does, in simple everyday words a 12-year-old would understand; no jargon",
           "customers": "who buys from it, in one simple sentence",
           "everyday": "one sentence linking it to something ordinary people know or use, or null",
           "money": [ {"part": "business line in simple words", "share": decimal share of sales or null, "plain": "what it sells there, in a few simple words", "tag": "main|new|moonshot"} ]  (its main ways of making money, largest first, up to 6; also include any new business line or one with explosive, moonshot potential even if its sales are still small. tag: "main" = an established line that brings in a large part of sales; "new" = launched or entered in roughly the last 3 years; "moonshot" = could grow many times over or reshape the company, e.g. a new technology or market, even if unproven. Give each line one tag, the one that fits best)},
 "summary": "2-3 plain-English sentences on whether and why it has a competitive advantage",
 "pricingPower": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "specific evidence, e.g. price rises and what happened to volumes"},
 "moats": [ {"source": one of ["Brand and intangible assets","Switching costs","Network effects","Cost advantage and scale","Efficient scale","Counter-positioning","Process power (hard-to-copy know-how)","Cornered resource (exclusive asset or talent)"], "strength": "strong|moderate|weak|none", "evidence": "one or two specific sentences"} ]  (all 8 sources, in that order),
 "customers": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "customer satisfaction and loyalty: retention, NPS, reviews, repeat purchase"},
 "talent": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "ability to attract and keep top talent: employer rankings, reputation, pay"},
 "product": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "is the product best in class? independent benchmarks, awards, ecosystem"},
 "competitors": [ {"name": "company name", "ticker": "main listing ticker (exchange suffix if not US, e.g. 005930.KS) or null if private",
                   "usTicker": "ticker of its US listing or ADR that files reports with the SEC, or null", "overlap": "high|medium|low",
                   "note": "where they compete"} ]  (every significant competitor, most direct first, up to 15; include major private ones with ticker null),
 "estimates": [ {"name": "company name", "fy": "FY2025", "currency": "USD", "revenueUSDm": number, "revenueGrowth3y": decimal, "grossMargin": decimal, "operatingMargin": decimal, "netMargin": decimal} ]
   (approximate latest fiscal-year figures for the company itself and for every listed competitor; decimals, e.g. 0.42; null if unknown),
 "marketShare": [ {"market": "market name", "measure": "revenue|units|shipments|...", "latestYear": "2025", "earlierYear": "2020",
                   "rows": [ {"name": "company name", "latest": decimal or null, "earlier": decimal or null} ] } ]  (up to 3 of its main markets, the company and its main rivals),
 "threats": ["specific things that could weaken its advantage"],
 "ceo": {"name": "current CEO", "founder": true or false, "since": "YYYY", "background": "e.g. electrical engineer, Stanford MBA"},
 "checklist": { "<id>": {"verdict": "yes|partly|no|unknown", "evidence": "one specific sentence with names, numbers or examples"} }  for EVERY id below:
   "c1": Rule Breaker #1: is it the leader of an important industry that is still emerging and growing fast?
   "c2": Rule Breaker #2: why do customers choose it over rivals (brand, better value, innovation, culture, leadership), and is that advantage hard to copy and likely to last many years?
   "c3": Rule Breaker #5: do ordinary people recognise the name, is it the default leader in its field (like Google, Amazon, NVIDIA, Tesla, Intuitive Surgical, Netflix), and would customers recommend its product?
   "c4": Does it have an inspiring mission it keeps emphasising, with management driven by purpose rather than money? If it spends 10 years doing this, would it matter?
   "c6": What is the general public consensus about the company and its products or services? When people hear the name, what are the first few descriptive words that come to mind? Start the evidence with those words in quotes (e.g. “innovative, premium, reliable”), then say whether that impression is mostly positive.
   "c7": Is its total addressable market large and growing, riding a secular trend (like CRWD, NVDA, TSLA, AMZN)?
   "c8": Does it have room to expand into big new markets: in its name, its technology or its vision?
   "m1": Is the CEO a visionary with a clear picture of the future?
   "m2": Is the CEO a founder (or acting like one): long-term thinking, working extraordinarily hard, pouring heart and soul into building something that outlives them?
   "m4": Does the CEO lead by serving employees and customers?
   "m5": Has the CEO deliberately built a strong, distinctive culture that keeps inventing new products and technologies?
   "m6": Is the CEO deeply hands-on with the product and technology, ideally with an engineering background?
   "m7": Is the CEO a person of great character who cares about something bigger than profit? For successor CEOs: is stewardship aimed at the benefit of humanity?
   "m7b": Has the CEO been invited to give a commencement speech at a top university (Stanford, Harvard, MIT, etc.)? Name it.
   "m8b": Does the CEO have a distinctive, memorable personality (like Elon Musk, Alex Karp, Larry Page)?
   "m9": Has the CEO a strong record of execution and results?
   "m10": Is the CEO and company known for frugality (like Bezos's door desk)?
   "c10": Do its products solve problems for people all over the world, greatly improving the lives of a very large number of people (like NFLX, GOOG, ISRG)?
   "p2": Is what it builds extremely hard to do, and important to the world?
   "f1": Has revenue grown in almost every one of the last five years?
   "f2": Have gross and operating margins risen over the last five years?
   "f3": Is debt low compared with cash and cash flow, with positive shareholders' equity?
   "f4": Have operating income and operating cash flow risen over the last five years?
   "v1": Is its main product clearly the best in its field, with a practical reason an ordinary person can understand for choosing it over every alternative (like NVIDIA over AMD)?
   "v2": Is it widely seen as one of the best companies to work for (culture, mission, reputation, employer rankings)? Cite rankings.
   "c5": Do its products make the world better? If it disappeared overnight, who would notice and miss it, and why?
 "asOf": "YYYY-MM of the newest information you used"
}

result.name: Trane Technologies plc
result.industry: Heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) and transport refrigeration
markets: Commercial HVAC (chillers, rooftop units, air handlers, controls) for offices, hospitals, schools, factories and data centers
Residential heating and cooling (Trane, American Standard brands) in North America
HVAC services, parts, building automation and energy services
Transport refrigeration for trucks, trailers and shipping containers (Thermo King)
Data-center thermal management, including chiller plants and liquid cooling

mission.statement: boldly challenge what's possible for a sustainable world
mission.source: Trane Technologies FY2025 Form 10-K (stated as the company's purpose)
mission.plain: Trane wants to push its products and its industry to cut energy use and climate-warming emissions.

about.plain: Trane Technologies makes big machines that heat and cool buildings, like the giant chillers on top of hospitals, offices and data centers, and the air conditioners and furnaces in many homes. It also makes the refrigerators on trucks and trailers that keep food and medicine cold on the road (Thermo King). After the machines are installed, it earns money fixing and maintaining them and running the software that controls them. It sells in more than 60 countries but most of its money comes from the Americas.
about.customers: Building owners, contractors, data-center operators, schools, hospitals, homeowners through dealers, and trucking and shipping companies.
about.everyday: The cool air in your school, the hospital or the cloud servers behind your phone apps, and the fridge-truck delivering your groceries may all come from a Trane or Thermo King machine.

money.plain: chillers, rooftop units, air handlers and controls for big buildings; the Americas segment, which includes it, was 80.5% of 2025 sales
repairs, maintenance contracts, parts and building-management software; management says roughly one-third of revenue
air conditioners, heat pumps and furnaces sold through dealers under Trane and American Standard
fridge units for trucks, trailers, vans and containers
large chiller plants and liquid-cooling systems for AI data centers, expanded by buying Stellar Energy (completed February 2026)
autonomous HVAC control software from BrainBox AI that tunes buildings to save energy

result.summary: Trane has a solid, widening competitive advantage built on its Trane and Thermo King brands, a dense direct sales and service network (over 7,500 technicians), and leadership in large commercial chillers, which has made it a preferred supplier for AI data centers. The result shows in gross margin rising from 30.5% in 2020 to 36.2% in 2025 and a record $12.1 billion backlog in mid-2026, though residential and transport are more cyclical and competitive.

pricingPower.evidence: Gross margin climbed every year from 30.5% (2020) to 36.2% (2025) while revenue grew from $12.45B to $21.32B, showing price increases stuck through the 2021-2023 inflation; even when residential volumes fell mid-teens in Q4 2025, management said residential pricing held, and 2026 guidance still assumes about 1.5 points of price on top of absorbing roughly $200M of tariff costs.

moats.evidence: Trane and Thermo King are century-old, trusted trade brands among engineers, contractors and fleet owners, and Trane has made FORTUNE's World's Most Admired Companies list 14 years running, but homeowners mostly choose through their dealer.

Installed chillers and building controls run 20+ years and nearly every major chiller project carries a service agreement, so owners tend to stay with Trane for parts, service and replacements, though new projects are competitively bid.
A larger customer base does not make Trane's equipment more valuable to other users.

With $21.3B of 2025 revenue, about $348M of R&D and a direct service force of over 7,500 technicians, Trane spreads engineering and service costs over a larger installed base than most rivals except Daikin and Carrier.
Large-chiller and transport-refrigeration markets have only a handful of global suppliers, but they are not natural monopolies and Asian makers keep adding capacity.
Trane's early, all-in bet on sustainability and electrified heat pumps (Gigaton Challenge) is hard for diversified rivals to copy quickly, but most peers are now pursuing the same strategy.

Decades of applied-systems engineering, quick-ship chiller capacity expanded more than 4x in two to three years, and a combined product-plus-service model (services about one-third of revenue) give it an execution edge on complex projects like data centers.
It owns no exclusive resource; refrigerant and component technologies are broadly available to competitors.

customers.evidence: Organic bookings rose 11% in 2025 and 37% in Q2 2026, with Americas applied-equipment bookings up 130% and a record $12.1B backlog, signalling heavy repeat business from large building and data-center owners; services, mostly recurring, have grown at a low-teens rate since 2020.

talent.evidence: Named to FORTUNE's World's Most Admired Companies for the 14th straight year (2026), Ethisphere's World's Most Ethical Companies (2026, third year) and JUST Capital's top company in Construction & Materials (2026), with an employee engagement score of 81 that it says is top quartile.

product.evidence: Trane is a leading supplier of large water-cooled chillers used in AI data centers, has the EcoWise line of low global-warming-potential refrigerant products, holds a CDP Climate 'A List' rating four years running, and Thermo King is a leading brand in truck and trailer refrigeration.

threats: A slowdown or pause in AI data-center construction would hit the fastest-growing part of its applied chiller orders and the record $12.1B backlog
Data-center designs shifting to warmer-water liquid cooling could reduce the need for large chillers
Residential HVAC is cyclical: Americas residential revenue fell mid-teens in Q4 2025 and was guided flat to down 5% for 2026
Tariffs and metal costs (about $200M of 2026 cost pressure expected after mitigation)
Asian rivals (Daikin, Midea, LG, Samsung) pushing into US heat pumps, VRF and data-center cooling
Refrigerant regulation changes that could make existing products non-compliant

ceo.name: Dave Regnery
ceo.background: Career-long company insider; finance degree from Northeastern University and MBA from Lehigh University; previously president and COO and head of Commercial HVAC and Thermo King

c1.evidence: Trane is a leader in a large, century-old industry (HVAC), but its fastest-growing niche, cooling AI data centers, is emerging quickly, helping push Q2 2026 bookings up 39% to $7.8B.

c2.evidence: Customers pick Trane for engineering reliability, efficient chillers and its direct service network of over 7,500 technicians; that is durable but Carrier, Daikin and JCI offer similar products.

c3.evidence: Many homeowners know the Trane name from home air conditioners, but it is not the single default leader in HVAC, where Daikin and Carrier are as large or larger.

c4.evidence: Its purpose to 'boldly challenge what's possible for a sustainable world' is repeated in every annual report and tied to the 2030 Gigaton Challenge to cut one billion metric tons of customer emissions, which would matter given buildings' large share of emissions.

c6.evidence: “reliable, durable, air conditioning, premium” - the impression from homeowners and contractors is mostly positive, with Trane seen as a well-built, higher-priced HVAC brand.

c7.evidence: HVAC is a market of well over $100B a year riding electrification (heat pumps), energy-efficiency rules, refrigerant transitions and AI data-center cooling, and Trane's 2026 guidance calls for about 11.5% revenue growth.

c8.evidence: It is expanding into data-center liquid cooling (Stellar Energy, 2026), AI building controls (BrainBox AI) and services, but stays within thermal management.

m1.evidence: Regnery has a clear, consistently stated vision of sustainable, electrified, digitally controlled buildings and positioned Trane early for data-center cooling, though he is more operator than visionary.

m2.evidence: Not a founder, but a career-long Trane/Ingersoll Rand insider who emphasises long-term investment and sustainability goals out to 2030 and beyond.

m4.evidence: He stresses an 'uplifting culture' and engagement (score of 81, top quartile), but there is little public evidence of a distinctive servant-leadership style.

m5.evidence: Trane has built a sustainability-centred culture and keeps launching products (EcoWise low-GWP line, quick-ship chillers, liquid cooling), though innovation is incremental rather than breakthrough.

m6.evidence: Regnery led product businesses (launched EcoWise as Commercial HVAC president) but trained in finance, not engineering.

m7.evidence: He sits on the World Economic Forum's Alliance of CEO Climate Leaders and has tied the company's strategy to cutting customers' emissions, with no known scandals.

m7b.evidence: No record found of a commencement speech by Dave Regnery at a top university.

m8b.evidence: Regnery is a low-key corporate CEO without a widely known public persona.

m9.evidence: Since he became CEO in July 2021, revenue rose from $14.1B (2021) to $21.3B (2025), operating margin from 14.3% to 18.6% and diluted continuing EPS from $5.96 to $13.14.

m10.evidence: Trane is not known for a frugal culture; it is run as a well-managed, cost-disciplined industrial without notable frugality traditions.

c10.evidence: Its products keep hospitals, homes, food and data centers at safe temperatures in more than 60 countries, but the benefit is indirect rather than a life-changing consumer product.

p2.evidence: Large, efficient chiller plants and transport refrigeration are hard engineering and important for health, food safety and computing, but several rivals can build them.

f1.evidence: Revenue rose every year from $12,454.7M (2020) to $14,136.4M, $15,991.7M, $17,677.6M, $19,838.2M and $21,321.9M (2025); 2020 was the only recent dip.

f2.evidence: Gross margin rose from 30.5% (2020) to 36.2% (2025) with one small dip in 2022, and operating margin rose every year from 12.3% to 18.6%.

f3.evidence: Debt of $4.6B against $1.3B cash (June 2026) is modest next to $3.2B of 2025 operating cash flow and $8.6B of equity, but debt still exceeds cash.

f4.evidence: Operating income rose every year from $1,532.8M (2020) to $3,967.4M (2025) and operating cash flow from $1,766.2M to $3,220.4M, though it dipped in 2021 and 2022.

v1.evidence: Trane is among the best large-chiller and commercial HVAC makers, but there is no single, obvious reason for an ordinary buyer to choose it over Carrier, Daikin or JCI.

v2.evidence: FORTUNE World's Most Admired Companies for 14 consecutive years (2026), Ethisphere World's Most Ethical Companies 2026 and JUST Capital's top company in its industry in 2026.

c5.evidence: Building owners, data-center operators and food shippers would notice quickly if it vanished, as a large share of chillers, rooftops and truck refrigeration units would lose parts and service, though rivals could eventually fill the gap.
